questions.q: When did you get your first mobile phone?
questions.answer: I got my first one when I started college, at around sixteen. It was a basic model that could only make calls and send texts, but I was absolutely [[thrilled]] with it, even though it seems ancient by today's standards.

questions.q: How often do you use your mobile phone?
questions.answer: Far too often, if I'm honest. It's become almost [[indispensable]] for work and staying in touch, so it's rarely out of my hand. Lately I've been trying to set limits, because it's easy to lose track of time.

questions.q: What do you mainly use your phone for?
questions.answer: Mostly for work, to be honest. I reply to students' messages, check emails and join video calls. Outside work, I read the news and keep in touch with my elder sister in Dhaka, so it's become a real [[lifeline]].

questions.q: Do you prefer phone calls or text messages?
questions.answer: For quick things, texting, since it's fast and doesn't interrupt anyone. But for anything important, I much prefer a call. You can hear the tone of someone's voice, which makes the exchange feel far more [[genuine]].

questions.q: Do you think young children should have smartphones?
questions.answer: Not at a very young age. A basic phone for emergencies is sensible, but [[unrestricted]] internet access can be harmful. I think parents should introduce smartphones gradually and keep an eye on how they're used.
